$comment: A derived template (packs/README.md 'Derived templates'): the care pack composed with an adult-psychology content seed and a steel-blue brand over the luxe-light register. Everything else — pages, sections, contract, tests — is the base pack's; compose expands this catalog through resolveCatalog (scripts/lib/pack-switch.mjs). Deliberately apart from the care-therapy remix: individual adult psychotherapy and assessment (doctoral clinicians, named methods, measurement-based care), not couples-and-families warmth.
title: Psychologist
description: An adult psychotherapy and assessment practice site built to read like the practice works: three doctoral psychologists with credentials and specialties, evidence-named services (ERP for OCD, behavioral activation, CBT-I), plain-language FAQs on cost and confidentiality, an in-network insurance strip, and real online booking — free consultations, intakes, 50-minute sessions, and three-hour assessment blocks projected from each psychologist's actual week, capacity-1, double-booking impossible. The booking form is deliberately clinically empty: name, contact, appointment type — why someone is seeking care never touches the site.

content.$comment: Business-content contract seed override. resolveCatalog merges a remix's content per-domain over the base's, so these practice and appointments seeds replace the base pack's at compose and mirror THIS remix's contentSeed module entry for entry (the remix-seed tests pin the twins) — the composed template's Manage editors and booking widget open on the psychology practice, not the base clinic.

providers.name: Dr. Naomi Adler
providers.bio: Twenty years treating anxiety disorders and OCD with exposure and response prevention — the treatment with the strongest evidence, done properly and paced humanely. Naomi founded Juniper Hill on one rule: every client knows the plan, the method, and the number we're watching.

providers.name: Dr. Marcus Osei
providers.bio: Marcus treats depression the way it actually lifts: behavioral activation first, thought work second, and a plan for the week you're in — not the person you're supposed to become. Half his caseload is men who waited years to call anyone.

providers.name: Dr. Priya Raghavan
providers.bio: Priya runs the practice's assessment service: ADHD, memory and attention concerns, and the diagnostic knots two prior providers couldn't untie. Full batteries, plain-language reports in two weeks, and a feedback session where you can ask anything.

services.name: Individual therapy
services.description: Weekly 50-minute sessions built on cognitive and behavioral methods — with goals you set, and progress you can see.

services.name: Anxiety & panic
services.description: Structured treatment for generalized anxiety, panic, and phobias — skills first, then practice in the situations that matter.

services.name: OCD treatment
services.description: Exposure and response prevention (ERP), the gold-standard treatment — collaborative, graded, and never sprung on you.

services.name: Depression
services.description: Behavioral activation and cognitive therapy for depression — small honest steps, measured weekly, that compound.

services.name: Adult ADHD assessment
services.description: A full testing battery, a clear yes-or-no answer, and a plain-language report you can take to any prescriber.

services.name: Psychological assessment
services.description: Diagnostic clarity when the picture is muddy — mood, attention, memory, personality — with a feedback session included.

services.name: Insomnia (CBT-I)
services.description: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia: four to eight sessions, no sleep hygiene lectures, real sleep-window work.

services.name: Telehealth sessions
services.description: Secure video sessions anywhere in Michigan and PSYPACT states — the same treatment, without the drive.

insurance: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan

reviews.quote: Dr. Adler told me in the first session exactly how ERP works, why it works, and what week four would feel like. Sixteen sessions later I drove over the bridge I'd been avoiding for six years — and then we graduated me, on schedule.
reviews.name: M. S.

reviews.quote: I'm 44 and had never told anyone I was struggling. Dr. Osei didn't make me perform sadness or explain my childhood before lunch — we made a plan for that week. The plan got bigger. So did I.
reviews.name: D. K.

reviews.quote: Two doctors and one internet quiz couldn't tell me if I had ADHD. Dr. Raghavan's report answered it in plain English, with the data attached, and the feedback session was worth the fee by itself.
reviews.name: R. T.

newPatient.title: Do you take insurance?
newPatient.body: We're in network with the plans listed above; for everything else we provide a superbill for out-of-network reimbursement. Session and assessment fees are on the confirmation email — no surprises at the door.

newPatient.title: Therapy or assessment — which do I book?
newPatient.body: If you want to work on something, book therapy. If you want to know what's going on — ADHD, memory, a diagnosis that never quite fit — book an assessment. If you're not sure, the free 15-minute call exists exactly for this question.

newPatient.title: What happens in the first session?
newPatient.body: You talk, we listen, and then we're honest with you: what we think is going on, which treatment has the best evidence for it, and how many sessions that usually takes. You leave with a plan and a baseline measure we'll track together.

newPatient.title: Is what I share confidential?
newPatient.body: Yes, with the legal exceptions every psychologist carries (safety, court orders), explained in plain language before you say a word. Booking online asks nothing about your reasons — that stays in the room.

types.name: Free 15-minute consultation
types.description: A short phone call to match you with the right psychologist — or point you elsewhere, honestly.

types.name: First session (intake)
types.description: A structured first hour: your history, a baseline measure, and a treatment plan with a number of sessions on it.

types.name: Therapy session
types.description: The standard 50-minute session — in the office or by secure video.

types.name: Assessment testing block
types.description: A three-hour testing block with breaks built in — most assessments need one or two.

theme.$comment: Steel blue over the luxe-light register's near-white ground — the care family's calm, credible light voice re-inked from clinical teal to a scholarly slate blue, visibly apart from the therapy remix's warm clay. mode light opens the site in its native daylight appearance; marketing pages resolve brand over preset accent, so the overlay re-inks pages and app surfaces together. navigation re-pins the shared careShell chrome (a declared theme variant outranks the shell prop): the base clinic wears the full-width administrative band and the therapy remix the centered masthead, so the psychology practice takes the split letterhead — the ruled, stationery read — per the nav-variety audit.
